solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Catholic office better put back in the money

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the word for wages

parts.note: pay is the money you earn

indicators.note: put back says the word for better is turned round, read right to left

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it

explanation.surface: A Catholic official is being told their job would pay better if returned to the funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns CAP into PAC, which goes 'in' PAY.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal office, the position of Pope, is the highest office of the Catholic Church.

clue.text: Mail company retaining sexy image

indicators.note: retaining means the mail company holds the word for sexy inside it

parts.note: PO, the Post Office, delivers the mail
hot is slang for sexy

explanation.surface: A postal company holds on to a racy picture.
explanation.walkthrough: PO is the Post Office, Britain's mail service.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot taken by a camera is an image, a picture of something.

clue.text: Adventurer, one occupying stretcher in Southend?

indicators.note: occupying means the word one sits within the structure

parts.note: Southend Pier stretches far out to sea, the longest pleasure pier in the world

explanation.surface: An adventurer lies on a stretcher in the seaside town of Southend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stretcher' suggests a medical one, but it is the pier, something that stretches out. Southend-on-Sea is an Essex resort famous for its very long pier.
explanation.definitionFit: An early explorer or settler going into new territory is an adventurer.

clue.text: Italian lace designed to cover a European up

indicators.note: to cover means the rearranged letters wrap around the other piece
designed means the letters are worked into a new pattern
up in a down clue means the word for European is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a Serb is a European from Serbia

explanation.surface: Italian lace made to cover a European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian' looks like it describes the lace, but it is the definition: the word means Calabrian and is also the name of a green broccoli.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means Calabrian, from Calabria in southern Italy, and names a broccoli.

clue.text: Front of shirt with Rwandan zip only closing — button it!

indicators.note: front of picks the opening letter of the word shirt

parts.note: the Hutu are the majority people of Rwanda

indicators.note: only closing picks just the final letter of the word zip

explanation.surface: A tailor describes a shirt from Rwanda whose zip only closes at the front, then tells someone to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zip' and 'button' look like dressmaking, but 'button it!' is the definition. HUTU is one of the peoples of Rwanda.
explanation.definitionFit: Button it is a colloquial order to stop talking, exactly the same rude command.

clue.text: Couple in difficulty

definitions.meaning: to couple means to fasten or hook together, as with a trailer
a snag or minor problem that holds things up

explanation.surface: A couple who are having problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple' looks like a pair of people, but it is the verb meaning to fasten.
explanation.definitionFit: Fastening a trailer to a car and a snag in plans both use this word.

clue.text: Not entirely quiet, about to criticise percussion

indicators.note: about means the shortened word goes round the word for criticise
not entirely means the final letter is dropped from the word for quiet

parts.note: timid, shy and retiring, means quiet
to pan a show is to criticise it harshly

explanation.surface: Someone not entirely quiet is about to criticise the percussion section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' cuts TIMID to TIMI, which goes 'about' PAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Kettledrums are the chief tuned percussion instruments of the orchestra.

clue.text: Imply the existence of power I created is crooked

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dishonest admission that the power someone created is corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is crooked' rearranges I CREATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert or assume something as a basis for reasoning implies it exists.

clue.text: U-turn of Tory seen through spy lens

indicators.note: seen through places one piece within the word for a spy, as if looked through

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation

indicators.note: U-turn of says the abbreviation for Tory is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, the Tory party

explanation.surface: A Tory politician's U-turn is watched through a spy's lens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'U-turn of' turns CON into NOC, which is 'seen through' MOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeglass for a single eye is a kind of lens, worn in the eye socket.

clue.text: Thrown out

definitions.meaning: thrown here means baffled or confused, at a loss for an answer
out in cricket when the wicketkeeper breaks the wicket while the batsman is out of the crease

explanation.surface: A short report that someone or something was ejected.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman who steps out of the crease can be put out when the wicketkeeper knocks the bails off; the same word means puzzled.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: puzzled people are thrown, and a cricketer dismissed by the keeper is out.

clue.text: Typically, Eliot's fourth, 'Murder in the Cathedral', perhaps?

indicators.note: fourth picks the letter in fourth place in the name Eliot

parts.note: taken literally, violence in a church could be fury in its main body, the nave

explanation.surface: A reference to T S Eliot's play Murder in the Cathedral as typical of his work.
explanation.walkthrough: The play's title is reread as NAVE RAGE, a fit of anger in a cathedral's nave, on the pattern of road rage; 'perhaps' flags the fanciful example.
explanation.definitionFit: As a rule or in the usual way, the idiom means typically.

clue.text: Darling, sweet thing given some flowers

parts.note: honey is a sweet thing made by bees
a bunch is a handful of flowers tied together

explanation.surface: A sweetheart is given a sweet treat and a bouquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet thing' seems another term of endearment like 'Darling', but it is honey.
explanation.definitionFit: A term of endearment for a loved one, used just as darling is.

clue.text: Central line where a figure pivots

definitions.meaning: a central straight line about which a shape is symmetrical
the line about which a rotating figure turns

explanation.surface: A description of the line a dancer or skater spins about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central line' may suggest the London Underground line, but it is the line through the middle of a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Geometry uses the word both for a line of symmetry and for the line of rotation.

clue.text: Try thorny flower, nothing less, as prickly plant

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: less means the letter for nothing is taken away from the flower

parts.note: the rose is the famous flower with thorns
O, a zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Advice to try a thorny flower in place of a prickly plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes O from ROSE, leaving RSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Furze, a spiny yellow-flowered shrub of heaths, is a prickly plant.

clue.text: Relative measure taken to shackle Italian leader, as pompous

parts.note: gran is a grandmother, a relative

indicators.note: to shackle means the measure holds the leading letter inside it

parts.note: a dose is a measured amount of medicine

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of Italian

explanation.surface: A relative takes measures to restrain an Italian leader, being pompous.
explanation.walkthrough: DOSE holds I, the first letter of Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy, imposing and self-important in manner, so the adjective means pompous.

clue.text: Pure alcoholic drink circulating quickly around

indicators.note: around shows the word for spreading fast goes round the drink

parts.note: something viral spreads rapidly online
gin is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: A pure spirit is being passed swiftly round a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pure' sits as an adjective describing the drink, but it is the definition, in the sense of chaste.
explanation.definitionFit: Untouched and chaste, like a maiden, so the adjective means pure.

clue.text: Conservative moral victory beginning to grate

parts.note: right means morally good
a win is a victory

indicators.note: beginning to picks the opening letter of the word grate

explanation.surface: A Conservative's moral victory starts to irritate others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative' looks like the Tory party, but it is an adjective here for politically to the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Conservative politics sit on the right side of the spectrum, hence the term.

clue.text: Turmoil in vehicle for African driver

indicators.note: in places the word for turmoil within the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a melee is a confused brawl or turmoil

explanation.surface: Chaos inside a car belonging to a driver in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' suggests a car, but this driver drives camels.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who drives camels, as in the deserts of North Africa, is a driver there.

clue.text: Water, perhaps, something heated in a kettle

definitions.meaning: water was one of the four classical substances, with earth, air and fire
the heating coil inside an electric kettle

explanation.surface: Water is the thing that gets heated in a kettle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites the obvious answer water, but the second definition is the kettle's coil.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient thought had four basic ones, water among them; a kettle's heating coil bears the same name.

clue.text: Old actress? That's not right — an old actor

indicators.note: not right says the letter R, for right, is removed from the actress's name

parts.note: Betty Grable was a Hollywood star of the 1940s

explanation.surface: Someone corrects a guess: it wasn't an old actress but an old actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing R from Betty GRABLE gives Clark Gable, star of Gone with the Wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Clark, the Hollywood leading man of the 1930s, was a famous film star of the past.

clue.text: Nothing arising, cutting plain scored mark

indicators.note: cutting means the reversed word goes into the word for plain

parts.note: bare means plain, unadorned

indicators.note: arising in a down clue means the word for nothing reads upwards

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing comes up, and a plain mark is cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' turns NIL into LIN, which goes into BARE. 'scored' means written in a musical score.
explanation.definitionFit: In printed music the vertical stroke dividing bars is a mark in the score.

clue.text: Advantage from deuce achieved, serving ace, by all conclusions

indicators.note: all conclusions takes the closing letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A tennis scene: getting advantage from deuce by serving an ace.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis, after deuce the next point won gives 'advantage', which makes the definition sit in the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight lead over a rival is an advantage, as in having the upper hand.

clue.text: Loading of barges, eight large orders

indicators.note: orders means the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Instructions for loading eight large barges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orders' rearranges EIGHT and LARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The transfer of cargo to or from ships by small flat boats is called by this name.

clue.text: August coming up, get cold drink

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: august as an adjective means majestic, regal

explanation.surface: When August arrives, have a cold drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'August' looks like the month but is the adjective, REGAL, turned round by 'coming up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chilled, light beer is the usual cold drink in a pub.

clue.text: A thousand pounds, good money in Africa

parts.note: the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: A thousand pounds is a good sum of money in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a thousand pounds is called by this word.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the word for a sum of one thousand pounds or dollars.

clue.text: Extraneous rule written by extremists in fiasco

indicators.note: written by puts the word for rule next to the other piece
extremists in picks the first and last letters of the word fiasco

parts.note: to reign is to rule

explanation.surface: A rule drawn up by extremists ends in disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: FO, the outer letters of fiasco, comes first, then REIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming from outside, not belonging to the thing itself, as foreign matter is extraneous.

clue.text: Enjoy every bit, mostly computerised

parts.note: to dig it is slang for enjoying something

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word for every bit is dropped

parts.note: every bit means all of it

explanation.surface: A recommendation to enjoy something almost completely, now in electronic form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Data handled as numbers by computers is in electronic form, so the adjective means computerised.

clue.text: Whole passage of statement I retracted

indicators.note: passage of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A speaker takes back the whole of a passage from an earlier statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retracted' sounds like a reversal signal, but the letters read forwards across 'statement I retracted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete, with nothing missing, is a straightforward synonym for whole.

clue.text: Old houses are needing no introduction, it's concurred

indicators.note: houses means the word for old holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: aged means old

indicators.note: needing no introduction means the first letter of are is removed

explanation.surface: Old houses that need no introduction are something everyone agrees on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing no introduction' cuts ARE to RE, which AGED 'houses'.
explanation.definitionFit: When something is concurred, all parties have settled it, so it is a settled matter.
